title: How to serve a built site with security headers
problem: My bundler writes a dist directory, and the static server I put in front of it sends none of the headers a production site needs unless I spell each one by hand, where a typo in a policy is silently ignored by the browser and a year-long cache lifetime can land on the wrong answer.
outcome: A Node.js process that serves the build with compression and entity tags, sends a framing policy, a permissions policy and cross-origin isolation declared as fields and refused at startup when malformed, caches hashed files for a year and makes pages revalidate, answers a missing file under the cached prefix with no-store in place of that lifetime, logs each request, answers a health probe and exits with code 0 on a terminate signal.

knowledge: A directory of built static files, such as the dist directory a bundler writes
Node.js 18 or later on the machine that serves it
A proxy or platform in front of the process that terminates TLS, since the server speaks plain HTTP
